chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Abu Thabit, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Is'haq, who said:

A mawla (client/freedman) of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) died. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Look, do you find an heir for him?' It was said to him: 'Two daughters for him in Al-Yamama, both slaves.' So he bought them both from the wealth of the deceased, then handed over to them the remainder of the wealth. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Thabit — similar to it.

key_terms.مَوْلًى: Mawla (client or freedman, a non-Arab convert or dependent in early Islamic society)

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a mawla distributed if his heirs are slaves?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of *wilayah* in inheritance, where Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) purchased the deceased mawla's slave daughters to emancipate them, thereby converting their status from slaves to free heirs. This act highlights the Imam's role in ensuring the spiritual and social dignity of his clients, linking the legal concept of inheritance with the moral imperative of manumission. It serves as a key precedent in Shia jurisprudence for how the Imam's estate can be utilized to secure the inheritance rights of mawali who might otherwise be excluded due to their enslaved status.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Abu Sabit, from hanan Bin Sudeyr, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Is’haq who said,

‘A slave of Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws died. Heasws said: ‘Look around, can you find an inheritor for him?’ So it was said to himasws, ‘There are two daughters for him at Al-Yamama, both slaves’. So heasws bought them both from the wealth of the deceased, then handed over to them the remainder of the wealth’. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Sabit - similar to it.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from abu Thabit from Hanan ibn Sadir from ibn abu Ya’fur from Ishaq who has narrated the following:

“A slave of Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, died. He said, ‘You must look if you can find his heirs.’ It was said that he has two daughters in Yamamah who are owned. He (the Imam) bought them from the assets of the deceased and gave the rest of legacy to them.’” Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from abu Thabit a similar Hadith.
